summary: The RTP specification has a registry of profile names used by higher-level protocols like SDP to refer to transport methods. This standards-track RFC registers new SDP transport protocol identifiers for carrying RTP media over TCP, covering several RTP profiles including DTLS and TLS variants.

plainLanguage.summary: Names for sending audio and video over TCP, written so call-setup messages can say which way they mean.

what is the sdp proto field
how to send rtp over tcp in sdp
subtitle: Seven new SDP names for carrying RTP media over TCP, plain, SRTP, DTLS-SRTP or TLS.

tldr.problem: SDP uses the proto field of an m= line to name the transport for a media stream, but no identifiers existed for several ways of sending RTP over TCP.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines and registers seven proto values, such as TCP/RTP/SAVPF and TCP/TLS/RTP/AVP. Each says which RTP profile and security layer is used over TCP, with RFC 4571 framing.
tldr.outcome: The values are registered by IANA in the proto subregistry of the SDP Parameters registry. They add no new security considerations beyond those of the transports they name.

today: RFC 7850 is a Proposed Standard published in April 2016, and it has not been obsoleted or updated by a later RFC.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
The Real-time Transport Protocol (RTP) carries real-time data such as audio or video, and the RTP Control Protocol (RTCP) monitors delivery. The Session Description Protocol (SDP, RFC 4566) describes multimedia sessions. RFC 4145 describes media over TCP in SDP, RFC 4571 defines how to frame RTP and RTCP packets on a connection-oriented transport such as TCP, and RFC 4572 adds TLS protection.

This RFC adds more SDP transport protocol identifiers for RTP media over TCP.
sections.plainLanguage: There are already some ways to send calls over a TCP connection. This RFC adds more names so everyone can say exactly which way they mean.

sections.title: The SDP m= Line and the proto Field
sections.content:
In SDP, the m= line describes a media stream, and its proto field names the transport protocol to use. The format is m=<media> <port> <proto> <fmt> ....

The RFC does not change this line. It only defines new values for the proto field.
sections.plainLanguage: A call setup message has a line that says what kind of thing is sent and how. The how part is the one that gets new names.

sections.title: The Seven New Identifiers
sections.content:
Each identifier combines TCP, an optional security layer and an RTP profile. All use the framing from RFC 4571.

  • TCP/RTP/AVPF: RTP media with RTCP-based feedback (RFC 4585) over TCP.
  • TCP/RTP/SAVP: Secure RTP (RFC 3711) over TCP.
  • TCP/RTP/SAVPF: Secure RTP with RTCP-based feedback (RFC 5124) over TCP.
  • TCP/DTLS/RTP/SAVP and TCP/DTLS/RTP/SAVPF: Secure RTP, without and with feedback, using DTLS-SRTP key establishment (RFC 5764) over TCP. DTLS-SRTP packets are framed as in RFC 4571.
  • TCP/TLS/RTP/AVP and TCP/TLS/RTP/AVPF: RTP media, without and with feedback, on top of TLS over TCP. Framed packets travel as application data messages over the TLS association set up as in RFC 4572.
sections.plainLanguage: Each name is like a recipe label: the kind of box, with or without a lock, and whether the receiver can send notes back about how it is going.

sections.title: ICE and TCP Candidates
sections.content: When the procedures of RFC 6544 are used to set up Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE, RFC 5245) candidates for a TCP transport, the framing from RFC 4571 MUST be used for STUN packets, which carry keepalives and consent checks.
sections.plainLanguage: When computers test which path works, even their little check messages must be packed in the same envelope format as the call data.

sections.title: IANA Registration
sections.content:
IANA registered all seven values in the proto subregistry of the Session Description Protocol (SDP) Parameters registry, each with RFC 7850 as the reference.

The Security Considerations section says the identifiers are mainly for the offer/answer model (RFC 3264) when negotiating RTP over TCP. The RFC adds no security considerations beyond those of the transports the identifiers name and those in Section 7 of RFC 4566.
sections.plainLanguage: The names went into the official list, and since they only name things that already exist, they bring no new dangers.
